# TESS Program G09180

Title: The Rotation.Age-Activity Relation From Wide Binaries

PI: Lares Martiz, Mariel - Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University

Type: SMALL

Summary: The rotation age relation is a cornerstone of stellar astrophysics, yet it is known to break down in key regimes, including the Kraft break, the weakened magnetic braking regime, the fully convective boundary, and the intermediate-period gap. These discrepancies limit the reliability of gyrochronology for field stars and propagate into uncertainties in stellar and exoplanet characterization. We propose to calibrate the rotation age activity relation using coeval wide binaries observed by TESS in Cycle 9. Wide binaries provide a controlled framework because their components share a common age and chemical composition while spanning a range of masses and magnetic regimes. By combining rotation periods, flare luminosities, and independently determined ages from asteroseismology or white-dwarf
